title: Echocardiographic Screening and Immunogenetic Characterization of Rheumatic Heart Disease in Migrant Populations in Germany
summary:
Background:

Rheumatic heart disease can develop as a consequence of an untreated or inadequately treated infection caused by certain bacteria. It can lead to permanent damage to the heart valves and, over time, cause serious heart problems. While the disease has become rare in Germany, it remains common in many parts of the world. People who have migrated to Germany from these regions may therefore have an increased risk of developing the disease. As rheumatic heart disease can remain without noticeable symptoms for many years, it often goes undetected.

Research Question:

The aim of this study is to investigate how frequently signs of rheumatic heart disease can be detected among people with a migration background living in Germany. The study also aims to explore whether certain characteristics of the immune system or inherited genetic traits are associated with the disease and could potentially contribute to its earlier detection.

Methods:

People aged 5 to 40 years who originate from selected regions with an increased risk of rheumatic heart disease or who have lived in these regions for an extended period may participate in the study.

Participants first complete a questionnaire about their health, country of origin, and living conditions. Basic health measurements are then taken, and the heart is examined using a portable ultrasound device. This examination is painless and takes only a few minutes.

If the initial examination reveals any abnormalities, a more detailed ultrasound examination of the heart at a hospital is offered. Participants with abnormal findings, as well as selected participants without abnormalities, will also provide a small blood sample and a saliva sample. These samples will be analyzed to investigate possible links between the disease, the immune system, and inherited genetic characteristics.

Depending on the examination results, participation involves one or two visits. No long-term follow-up is planned.

Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants are individuals aged ≥ 5 and ≤ 40 years who were born in one of the countries or regions exhaustively listed in Table 1 or who have resided in one of these countries or regions for a cumulative period of at least five years. The selection of countries and regions is based on the endemicity of rheumatic heart disease (RHD) as described by Watkins et al. (2017) or, for the additionally included regions in Türkiye, on regional echocardiographic prevalence data (Ozer et al., 2009; Atalay et al., 2019).

Table 1:
Africa: Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Côte d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Libya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Africa, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe.

South and Central Asia: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Kyrgyzstan, Nepal, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan.

East and Southeast Asia: Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar, Philippines, Timor-Leste.

Middle East: Iraq, Syria, Yemen.

Indian Ocean: Maldives.

Pacific and Oceania: Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Vanuatu.

Caribbean, Central America, and Northern South America: Belize, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname.

Europe and Caucasus: Albania, Azerbaijan, Georgia.

Türkiye (restricted to the following regions): Southeastern Anatolia Region and Ankara Province.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals will be excluded from the study if at least one of the following criteria applies:
- Age below 5 or above 40 years.
- None of the specified geographical or accommodation-related inclusion criteria are met.
- Known valvular heart disease of clearly non-rheumatic origin, such as congenital valvular heart disease, degenerative valvular heart disease, or a history of infective endocarditis.
- Lack of written informed consent from the participant or, in the case of minors, from their legal guardian(s).
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent in adult participants.
- Insufficient understanding of the essential study information required for informed consent, despite the provision of appropriate written translations or assistance from an interpreter.
- Previous participation in the RHED-MIG study.
